items.title: [MacRumors] iOS 27 Finally Unlinks Alarm Volume From Your iPhone Ringer
items.content_html:
For the better part of two decades, an iPhone's alarm volume has matched its ringer. In other words, if you slide the ringtone volume down to silence your iPhone overnight, you're also turning your alarm's volume down with it. That's no longer the case in iOS 27.


Settings now includes an "Alarms and Timers" section with its own Match Ringtone Volume toggle. If you toggle it off, a dedicated slider appears that allows you to drop the ringer volume to nothing, and you'll still be woken at whatever alarm volume you choose.

How to Set a Separate Alarm Volume



  1. Open Settings on your iPhone.

  2. Tap Sounds & Haptics.

  3. Under "Alarms and Timers," toggle off Match Ringtone Volume.

  4. Drag the slider that appears to set your alarm and timer volume.



That's all there is to it. Alarms and timers now have their own level, regardless of how quiet or loud your iPhone's ringer is set at.

Bear in mind that alarms carrying their own volume control – like any wake-up alarm you have selected in your Sleep schedule – will keep the level you set for them individually. To go back to the old behavior, simply toggle Match Ringtone Volume back on, and the slider will disappear.

A Second Toggle for Alerts and System Sounds


You may notice that directly below the "Alarms and Timers" controls sits a second Match Ringtone Volume switch in a separate section. This covers alerts and system sounds, like incoming texts, keyboard clicks, and suchlike. Toggle off this setting and you'll get a similar independent slider. It's a neat fix if, say, you've ever wanted a loud ringer without a loud keyboard.

iOS 27 is currently available in public beta and is expected to be generally available this coming September.

items.title: [Kagi Small Web] Night owls and early birds
items.content_html:
🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

🎨 🌾 🔧 🪶 🌲 🏔️ 🔭 ✏️

As young kids, most of us were up at 6 am, raring to go on weekend mornings. As teenagers, many of us slept in until late morning or noon. But people are different. Some love Marmite, some hate it. As adults, we start finding what works best for us. And it’s not necessarily the same as, or what works best for, our partners.

It struck me that I know a lot of couples, us included, who are night-owl/early-bird combos.

One of the couple naturally wakes at dawn and tiptoes out of bed. They’ve usually managed a host of morning peaceful time, exercise or chores before the night owl surfaces, often bleary-eyed.

And while the early bird crashes out in the evening, maybe falling asleep on the sofa, the night owl is often just getting going, hitting their productive stride, staying out, or watching late-night TV, before tiptoeing into bed next to the sleeping early bird.

Of course, we notice and talk about the differences. So perhaps there are a host of early-bird couples and night-owl couples. But eventually we all settle into the rhythms that work best for us, and I’m pretty sure I see a lot of opposites.

I can’t help wishing I were naturally an early bird on the same schedule as my wife. But perhaps it’s a combo that creates time for both partners and secretly a recipe for success?

As Kahlil Gibran wrote in The Prophet:

"And stand together yet not too near together:

  For the pillars of the temple stand apart,

  And the oak tree and the cypress grow not in each other's shadow."

Are you a night owl living with an early bird, or vice versa? How do you make it work for you?
